page: Amazon Web Services d3.2xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual server built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache, with instruction set support including AVX and AVX-512 extensions. The server includes 64 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources include 11,880 GB of attached local HDD storage, 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and zero discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate performance characteristics aligned with high-throughput sequential execution rather than burst compute. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves 6,744.33 on multi-core performance alongside a PassMark CPU score of 7,914.79, landing in the middle 50% band. Large-block memory bandwidth sustains 51.95 GB/sec for read operations and 41.01 GB/sec for write operations. Conversely, single-core processing is modest, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,117.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 22.65 GB/sec. Machine learning benchmarks reflect clear boundaries, yielding weak execution speeds for 7B parameter models due to the absence of specialized accelerators.

The qualitative efficiency profile of the d3.2xlarge is defined by its massive volume of local magnetic storage paired with stable compute capacity. By utilizing mechanical HDD media rather than expensive NVMe arrays, the platform delivers high capacity per node at lower cost per gigabyte for sequential read and write operations. The architectural tradeoff is limited random I/O performance compared to solid-state alternatives. This hardware configuration is optimal for distributed file systems such as HDFS, massive log aggregation, data warehousing staging nodes, batch ETL operations, and long-term sequential data retention pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services d3.2xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The configuration supplies 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 64 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, and an expansive 11,880 GB array of local HDD storage. Network throughput is provisioned with a 6 Gbps baseline, and the instance operates without a discrete GPU. In standardized benchmarking, the system displays middle-tier performance across multi-core compute workloads, memory bandwidth operations, and static web serving throughput, while single-core processing and compression throughput fall into lower tiers. Providing high storage density per compute thread, the instance offers economical resource scaling for sequential data access patterns. It is tailored for large-scale distributed file systems, data lake warehousing, log aggregation, and sequential data processing pipelines.
